result.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
result.summary: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards. To overcome this, we introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module. Our search samples $K$ candidate tactics at each step and repairs a failed tactic at most $R$ times. Instead of discarding failed tactics, we feed the compiler's error message to a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps in place. This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark. Repair is not free: it trades extra runtime for reachable proofs. But the trade is predictable: repair pays most when sampling is constrained; its return is front-loaded, with the first repair attempt capturing $84\text{--}96\%$ of the total gain; and the gain comes almost entirely from shallow tactic-execution failures rather than structural errors such as type mismatches. This targeted repair successfully replicates on a second benchmark (Lean Workbook), nearly doubling the solve rate with zero regressions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 Lean 4 自动定理证明中引入有界在线步级修复模块：每个推理步采样 K 个候选 tactic，失败时不丢弃，而是把编译器错误信息交给预训练修复模型就地修补至多 R 次，从而以额外运行时间换取更高求解率，并分析了修复收益前置与错误类型差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「采样—验证—预算内修复」的步级循环和对外部验证器错误信号的利用，可能为 LVR 中筛选并修补中间推理状态、以及在收益递减时决定继续还是停止提供方法线索，但其文本证明场景下的预算收益规律能否迁移尚需核查。
